related_questions.question: How long can you have herpes without knowing?

text_blocks.snippet: A person can have herpes without knowing for years, even decades, as it can remain dormant and asymptomatic. Many people with herpes never experience any symptoms or have such mild symptoms that they go unnoticed. While the initial outbreak typically occurs within 2-20 days after exposure, subsequent outbreaks can be infrequent or absent, and some individuals never experience any symptoms at all.

list.title: Dormancy:
list.snippet: Herpes simplex virus (HSV), both type 1 and type 2, can lie dormant in the body for extended periods.

list.title: Asymptomatic Infection:
list.snippet: Many people with herpes are unaware they are infected because they don't experience noticeable symptoms.

list.title: Variable Symptom Severity:
list.snippet: The severity of outbreaks can vary greatly, with some individuals experiencing frequent and painful outbreaks, while others have mild or no noticeable symptoms.

list.title: Transmission:
list.snippet: Even without symptoms, individuals with herpes can still transmit the virus to others.

list.title: Testing:
list.snippet: If you're concerned about herpes, it's important to get tested, as the virus can be present even without noticeable symptoms.

list.snippet: Itching, tingling, or burning sensation in the genital area
Small, painful blisters that may appear as red bumps or sores
Open sores that may bleed or ooze
Swollen lymph nodes in the groin
Mouth sores (if the virus spreads to the mouth)
Recurring outbreaks, which may become less severe over time
